*Settling in to think about the year ahead...*

Eh, another year. My back still hurts from last fall's sunflower harvest but what can I do, the land doesn't farm itself. My son is working in town at the factory and my daughter-in-law helps when she can. My husband helps with the heavy work but he's slow now too. So it's mostly me in the field.

I have 8.5 mu. For many years now I keep about 3 mu for wheat and maize — that little piece near the house with the better soil, I plant wheat in autumn and then maize right after the wheat comes off. The other 5.5 mu, the bigger piece farther out, I put in sunflower. Sunflower is less work than maize and the price has been alright the last few years. My neighbor Old Wang does the same on his land and he says the buyer from the oil press comes right to the village.

**For the wheat** (3 mu, going in this October after the maize): I do what I always do. Before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer on each mu — the 15-15-15 kind my son-in-law picks up at the agricultural supply shop in town. That's about one bag per mu, maybe 40 kg. Then in spring when the wheat is standing up and starts to look a bit yellow, I put down half a bag of urea per mu, maybe 20 kg. My husband says we should give more but fertilizer keeps getting more expensive and I don't want to waste money if the rain comes good.

Water — we have the well, but the electricity meter on it eats money. I'll irrigate before winter like always, that's one. Then in spring at jointing, that's two. If May gets dry I do one more before filling. Three irrigations most years.

Last year I got maybe 450 jin per mu — 450 jin, that's... about 225 kg? No wait, 1 jin is half a kg, so that's 225 kg per mu. Hmm, but the bag said I harvested about 900 jin from the three mu total. Anyway it was a decent year. I'll plan for the same.

**For the maize** (3 mu, planted right after wheat comes off in June): Very tight time between wheat harvest and maize planting — maybe 5 days, a week. I hire the neighbor with the small tractor to run through and plant in one pass, he puts the seed and the compound fertilizer together. One bag of compound per mu, same kind. Then when the maize is about knee-high I spread some urea by hand around the rows, half a bag per mu or a bit less. That's usually enough.

I don't irrigate maize unless July and August go completely dry. The summer rain usually comes. If the leaves curl I'll run water once.

Seed I buy from the shop — the yellow bag hybrid, I forget the name but it's the one everyone buys. Not the cheapest, not the most expensive.

**For the sunflower** (5.5 mu, planted end of May or early June): This is my main piece. Sunflower doesn't need as much as maize. I plow it once in spring with the hired tractor, then plant. I put compound fertilizer at planting — maybe two-thirds of a bag per mu, I'm careful with it because five and a half mu takes a lot of fertilizer and the money adds up fast. I don't topdress sunflower usually, just let it grow.

I irrigate sunflower once after planting to make sure it comes up, and maybe once more when the heads are forming if it's dry. That's it.

Pests — sunflower gets the moth sometimes, the one that eats the heads. If I see them I spray. I buy a small bottle at the shop. Weeds between the rows I hoe myself in June, that's a lot of bending but I do a little every morning before it gets hot.

Last year sunflower gave me around 400 jin per mu — 200 kg. Price was 4.5 yuan per jin. Not bad.

**Money-wise** — every year I worry. Fertilizer for all this land is the big expense. I stretch it where I can on the sunflower and don't cut corners on the wheat because wheat is our food. We keep back enough wheat to eat and to give to my daughter's family.

I'm not going to try anything new this year. When Old Wang's brother tried that new maize seed two years ago half his field didn't come up. At my age I can't afford to lose a crop.
